directory.description: The output directory every scheduled capture in this document writes into, and where manifest.json (the puck.parity.manifest.v1 document) lands once at least one capture has landed — relative to the process's current directory unless rooted. A --capture-dir boot flag overrides this for a deployment run (the --state-dir pattern), so two backend legs of the same document can target sibling directories without two document copies.

rows.description: The scheduled stations. Station names are unique; capacity MaxRows.

items.description: One tick-scheduled capture station: a stable name, the exact engine ticks it arms a composed-frame capture at, and the palette its per-pixel census sorts against. A station carries no camera reference of its own — what the composed frame shows at a given tick is the document's own doing (a state row plus rules driving a camera program's select op; see docs/views.md), so two backends that step the identical document capture the identical moment by construction, and this row only says WHEN to look, never AT WHAT.

station.description: The stable name — the manifest's station field and the frame filename's own prefix (<station>-<tick>.png). A WorldCellName: dot-free, non-empty, free of the reserved character set.

ticks.description: The exact simulation ticks (completed-tick coordinates, ascending, none repeated) this station arms a capture at. Capacity: MaxTicksPerRow.

palette.description: The per-pixel census's material table — at least one entry, at most MaxPaletteEntriesPerRow, unique Material indices.

items.description: One material bucket a capture's per-pixel census sorts against: the nearest-color match in a station's authored palette, since the composed render target carries pixel colors, not a per-pixel material-id buffer, and this is the mechanically honest fallback the render path actually supports (see Puck.World.WorldCaptureScheduler's own remarks for the exact matching rule).

material.description: The material's index — the manifest's census key. Author-chosen, unique within a row; not read against any other section's material table.

color.description: The material's reference color, #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA (alpha ignored — the composed frame carries none).
